decisions.reason: A pit (bor) was a dug cistern for storing water, sometimes used as a prison (Genesis 37:24). It is also a picture of the grave and the world of the dead (Psalm 28:1; 88:5).

decisions.choice: the pit: Jeremiah in the cistern
decisions.reason: Jeremiah was let down into a muddy cistern to die (Jeremiah 38:6); his story may lie behind verses 53-55.

decisions.choice: a stone: probably one stone over the mouth of the pit
decisions.reason: The word is singular. They may have closed the pit with a stone (compare Daniel 6:18), or thrown stones down at him.

decisions.choice: thrust me into the pit to end my life
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the pit first and say what it was for (m1).

records.literal_gloss: Have flowed waters over my head; I said, I am cut off.

en.L: Waters flowed over my head; \q I said, "I am cut off."
en.B: The waters rose over my head, \q and I said, "I am cut off!"
en.R: Water covered my head, \q and I thought, "This is the end of me!"

pt.L: Águas correram sobre a minha cabeça; \q eu disse: "Fui cortado."
pt.B: As águas subiram acima da minha cabeça, \q e eu disse: "Estou acabado!"
pt.R: A água cobriu a minha cabeça, \q e eu pensei: "É o meu fim!"

decisions.choice: waters over my head: being overwhelmed, close to death
decisions.reason: Deep water that covers the head is a picture of mortal danger and of the world of the dead (Psalm 69:2-3; 88:8; Jonah 2:6).

decisions.choice: I am cut off: from life and from God
decisions.reason: To be cut off (nigzar) is to be cut away from the land of the living and from God's care (Psalm 88:6; Isaiah 53:8).

decisions.choice: I thought, "This is the end of me!"
decisions.reason: Readable says what being cut off means here, and that he said it to himself.

records.literal_gloss: I called your name, Yahweh, from [the] pit of [the] lowest depths.

en.L: I called on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, \q from the lowest pit.
en.B: I called on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, \q from the bottom of the pit.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I called out to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} \q from deep down in the pit.

pt.L: Invoquei o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} nome, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, \q desde a cova mais profunda.
pt.B: Clamei pelo {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} nome, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, \q do fundo da cova.
pt.R: {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, eu clamei a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} \q lá do fundo do poço.

decisions.choice: nineteenth letter: qoph (verses 55-57)
decisions.reason: Verses 55-57 each begin with qoph, the nineteenth letter of the Hebrew alphabet (see verse 1).

decisions.choice: I called ... you heard (verses 55-61): his rescue told as past
alternatives: prayers for help: 'I call ... hear my voice'
decisions.reason: The verbs in verses 55-61 are in the form that usually tells what has happened: he called, God heard and came near and rescued him. Some read them instead as prayers ('hear my voice!'), a use of this form found in some psalms. Here they are taken as his memory of God's answer, which gives him confidence for the pleas of verses 59 and 63-66.

decisions.choice: called on your name: prayed to the LORD by name
decisions.reason: To call on the LORD's name is to pray to him and ask his help (Psalm 116:4).

decisions.choice: the lowest pit: the deepest place, near death
decisions.reason: The pit of verse 53, called 'lowest' as in Psalm 88:7, where the same words describe the depths of death.

decisions.choice: called out to you
decisions.reason: Readable says 'called out to you' for 'called on your name' (m3).

source.text: קוֹלִ֖י שָׁמָ֑עְתָּ אַל־תַּעְלֵ֧ם אָזְנְךָ֛ לְרַוְחָתִ֖י לְשַׁוְעָתִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: My voice you heard: do not hide your ear to my relief, to my cry for help.

en.L: You heard my voice: \q "Do not hide {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ear from my [plea for] relief, from my cry for help!"
en.B: You heard my voice: \q "Do not shut {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ears to my plea for relief, to my cry for help!"
en.R: You heard me when I begged, \q "Do not stop listening when I cry for help!"

pt.L: Tu ouviste a minha voz: \q "Não escondas o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} ouvido do meu [pedido de] alívio, do meu grito por socorro!"
pt.B: Tu ouviste a minha voz: \q "Não feches os {{deity_pronoun:teus|Teus}} ouvidos ao meu pedido de alívio, ao meu grito por socorro!"
pt.R: Tu me ouviste quando supliquei: \q "Não deixes de me ouvir quando eu grito por socorro!"

decisions.choice: you heard: and then the words of his prayer
decisions.reason: After 'you heard my voice' the man quotes what he prayed. The prayer may also be his plea now: 'hear my voice; do not hide your ear.'

decisions.choice: relief: breathing room, rescue
decisions.reason: The word (rewachah) means relief, a chance to breathe again (Exodus 8:11). Some take it as 'my sighing' or 'my breath', his gasping prayer.

decisions.choice: hide your ear: refuse to listen
decisions.reason: To hide or close one's ear is the opposite of hearing (Isaiah 1:15 uses 'hide the eyes' in the same way).

decisions.choice: Do not stop listening
decisions.reason: Readable says what 'hide your ear' means and folds the two phrases into one.

records.literal_gloss: You drew near on [the] day I called you; you said: do not fear.

en.L: You drew near on the day I called {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} said, "Do not fear!"
en.B: On the day I called to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} came close \q and said, "Do not be afraid!"
en.R: When I called to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} came close to me. \q You said, "Do not be afraid!"

pt.L: Tu {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} aproximaste no dia em que {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} chamei; \q {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} disseste: "Não temas!"
pt.B: No dia em que clamei a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} chegaste perto \q e disseste: "Não tenhas medo!"
pt.R: Quando clamei a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} chegaste perto de mim. \q Tu disseste: "Não tenhas medo!"

decisions.choice: Do not fear: God's word of rescue
decisions.reason: The two words are the LORD's promise to his people when he comes to save (Isaiah 41:10, 14; 43:1; Jeremiah 30:10). They are the only words of God quoted in the whole book.

decisions.choice: you drew near: God's presence answers the cry
decisions.reason: God drawing near is his help and favor (Psalm 145:18); it answers the cloud that shut out prayer (verse 44).

decisions.choice: When I called to you
decisions.reason: Readable puts the time clause first.

source.text: רַ֧בְתָּ אֲדֹנָ֛י רִיבֵ֥י נַפְשִׁ֖י גָּאַ֥לְתָּ חַיָּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: You have pleaded, Lord, [the] cases of my soul; you have redeemed my life.

en.L: You have pleaded, Lord, the cases of my soul; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have redeemed my life.
en.B: Lord, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have argued my case for me \q and redeemed my life.
en.R: Lord, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have stood up for me in court. \q You have rescued my life.

pt.L: Tu defendeste, Senhor, as causas da minha alma; \q {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} redimiste a minha vida.
pt.B: Senhor, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} defendeste a minha causa \q e redimiste a minha vida.
pt.R: Senhor, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} me defendeste no tribunal. \q Tu salvaste a minha vida.

decisions.choice: twentieth letter: resh (verses 58-60)
decisions.reason: Verses 58-60 each begin with resh, the twentieth letter of the Hebrew alphabet (see verse 1).

decisions.choice: pleaded the cases: taken up his cause as his advocate
decisions.reason: The verb and noun (riv) are used of a lawsuit. God has acted as the man's defender in court against those who wronged him (verse 36), as in Psalm 43:1 and Jeremiah 50:34.

decisions.choice: redeemed: acted as the man's next of kin to set him free
decisions.reason: The verb (ga'al) is what a close relative did for a family member in trouble: buy back his land or freedom, or defend him (Leviticus 25:25; Proverbs 23:11). God has done this for the man's life. Jeremiah 50:34 joins the same two ideas: 'their Redeemer is strong ... he will surely plead their case.'

decisions.choice: the cases of my soul: the cases that concern his very life
decisions.reason: The soul (nefesh) is his life, in parallel with 'my life' in the second line.

decisions.choice: rescued
decisions.reason: Isaiah's Readable has 'bought back' for this verb; here, where the picture is a legal defender and not a payment, Readable says 'rescued' (m3).

decisions.choice: my case / stood up for me in court
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say 'my case' or 'me' for 'the cases of my soul' (m4).

records.literal_gloss: You have seen, Yahweh, my wrong; judge my case!

en.L: You have seen, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, the wrong done to me; \q judge my case!
en.B: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have seen how I have been wronged; \q give judgment in my case!
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have seen how I have been wronged. \q Now judge my case and set things right!

pt.L: Tu viste, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, o mal feito a mim; \q julga a minha causa!
pt.B: {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} viste como fui injustiçado; \q faze justiça na minha causa!
pt.R: {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} viste como fui tratado com injustiça. \q Agora julga a minha causa e põe as coisas no lugar!

decisions.choice: the wrong done to me: injustice
decisions.reason: The word ('awwatah) is found only here; it is from the verb 'wrong' of verse 36, twisting someone's case.

decisions.choice: judge my case: decide for me, give me justice
decisions.reason: To ask a judge to judge one's case is to ask him to decide it rightly, and so in one's favor (Psalm 7:9; 26:1).

decisions.choice: and set things right
decisions.reason: Readable says what asking for judgment means here (m2).

records.literal_gloss: You have seen all their vengeance, all their plans against me.

en.L: You have seen all their vengeance, \q all their plans against me.
en.B: You have seen all their spite, \q all their schemes against me.
en.R: You have seen how they want revenge on me \q and all their plans to hurt me.

pt.L: Tu viste toda a vingança deles, \q todos os planos deles contra mim.
pt.B: Tu viste todo o rancor deles, \q todas as tramas deles contra mim.
pt.R: Tu viste como eles querem se vingar de mim \q e todos os planos que fazem para me prejudicar.

decisions.choice: their vengeance: their desire to pay him back
decisions.reason: The word (neqamah) is vengeance or revenge. Here it is the enemies' spite toward him, not God's just repayment that the man asks for in verses 64-66.

decisions.choice: plans: schemes, plots
decisions.reason: The word (machashavah) is a thought or plan, here plots against him (Jeremiah 11:19; 18:18).

records.literal_gloss: You have heard their reproach, Yahweh, all their plans against me,

en.L: You have heard their reproach, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, \q all their plans against me,
en.B: You have heard their insults, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, \q all their schemes against me,
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have heard their insults \q and all their plans against me.

pt.L: Tu ouviste a afronta deles, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, \q todos os planos deles contra mim,
pt.B: Tu ouviste os insultos deles, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, \q todas as tramas deles contra mim,
pt.R: {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ouviste os insultos deles \q e todos os planos deles contra mim.

decisions.choice: twenty-first letter: shin (verses 61-63)
decisions.reason: Verses 61-63 each begin with shin, the twenty-first letter of the Hebrew alphabet (see verse 1).

decisions.choice: verses 61-62 are one sentence
decisions.reason: 'You have heard' governs the lips and the muttering of verse 62 as well.

decisions.choice: reproach: taunts, scorn
decisions.reason: The word (cherpah) is the disgrace of verse 30, now in the mouths of his enemies.

records.literal_gloss: [the] lips of those rising against me and their muttering against me all the day.

en.L: the lips of those who rise against me, \q and their muttering against me all the day.
en.B: what my attackers say, \q and how they whisper against me all day long.
en.R: You have heard what my attackers say \q and how they whisper about me all day long.

pt.L: os lábios dos que se levantam contra mim, \q e o murmúrio deles contra mim o dia todo.
pt.B: o que dizem os que me atacam, \q e como cochicham contra mim o dia inteiro.
pt.R: Tu ouviste o que dizem os que me atacam \q e como cochicham sobre mim o dia inteiro.

decisions.choice: the lips of those who rise against me: what his attackers say
decisions.reason: Lips stand for speech. 'Those who rise against me' are his attackers or opponents (Psalm 3:2).

decisions.choice: muttering: low talk, scheming
decisions.reason: The word (higgayon) is a low murmur or quiet talk (Psalm 9:17), here whispered plots against him.

decisions.choice: You have heard
decisions.reason: Readable repeats the verb of verse 61 so that the verse can stand as a sentence.

records.literal_gloss: Their sitting and their rising, look; I [am] their mocking song.

en.L: Their sitting down and their rising up—look! \q I [am] their mocking song.
en.B: Look at them, whether they sit or rise: \q I am the song they mock me with.
en.R: Look at them! Whether they sit or stand, \q they sing songs to make fun of me.

pt.L: O sentar-se deles e o levantar-se deles — olha! \q Eu [sou] a canção de zombaria deles.
pt.B: Olha para eles, quer se sentem, quer se levantem: \q eu sou a canção com que zombam de mim.
pt.R: Olha para eles! Sentados ou em pé, \q eles cantam músicas para zombar de mim.

decisions.choice: sitting and rising: all they do, all day
decisions.reason: Sitting down and getting up together mean all of a person's life and activity (Deuteronomy 6:7; Psalm 139:2). In everything they do, they mock him.

decisions.choice: their mocking song: as in verse 14
decisions.reason: The same root as the mocking song of verse 14, and of Job 30:9.

decisions.choice: they sing songs to make fun of me
decisions.reason: Readable turns 'I am their mocking song' into what they do.

source.text: תָּשִׁ֨יב לָהֶ֥ם גְּמ֛וּל יְהוָ֖ה כְּמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יְדֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: You will return to them recompense, Yahweh, according to [the] work of their hands.

en.L: Give back to them [their] recompense, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, \q according to the work of their hands.
en.B: Pay them back, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, as they deserve, \q for what their hands have done.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, pay them back \q for the evil things they have done.

pt.L: Dá-lhes de volta [a sua] retribuição, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, \q segundo a obra das suas mãos.
pt.B: Paga-lhes, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, como merecem, \q pelo que as suas mãos fizeram.
pt.R: {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, dá a eles o que merecem \q pelas coisas más que fizeram.

decisions.choice: twenty-second letter: taw (verses 64-66)
decisions.reason: Verses 64-66 each begin with taw, the twenty-second letter of the Hebrew alphabet (see verse 1).

decisions.choice: you will return: a plea, 'pay them back'
decisions.reason: The verbs of verses 64-66 have the form 'you will', which here expresses a wish or plea, as the ancient Greek translation also takes them: the man asks God to act. They can also be read as confident statements: 'you will pay them back'.

decisions.choice: according to the work of their hands: the words of Psalm 28:4
decisions.reason: The psalmist prays in nearly the same words that the wicked receive what their deeds deserve (Psalm 28:4; compare Jeremiah 51:6, 24).

decisions.choice: a plea for justice, left in God's hands
decisions.reason: The man does not take revenge himself; he asks the LORD, the judge of verse 59, to repay. Scripture gives vengeance to God (Deuteronomy 32:35; Romans 12:19). The prayer asks for justice against those who destroyed his people, as in Jeremiah 11:20 and 18:21-23.

decisions.choice: the evil things they have done
decisions.reason: Readable says what the work of their hands is here.

records.literal_gloss: You will give to them covering of heart; your curse [be] on them.

en.L: Give them a covering of heart; \q {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} curse [be] on them!
en.B: Give them a veiled and hardened heart; \q let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} curse be on them!
en.R: Make them stubborn and blind. \q Put {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} curse on them!

pt.L: Dá-lhes uma cobertura de coração; \q a {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} maldição [esteja] sobre eles!
pt.B: Dá-lhes um coração velado e endurecido; \q que a {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} maldição caia sobre eles!
pt.R: Torna-os teimosos e cegos. \q Põe a {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} maldição sobre eles!

decisions.choice: a covering of heart: a mind veiled and hardened
decisions.reason: The word (meginnah) is found only here. It probably comes from a root meaning to cover or shield, so 'a covering of the heart' would be a heart closed and blind, unable to understand (compare Isaiah 6:10). Others relate it to grief and read 'anguish of heart'.

decisions.choice: your curse: God's judgment pronounced on them
decisions.reason: The word (ta'alah) is found only here; it is related to the common word for a curse or oath. It is the opposite of blessing.

decisions.choice: stubborn and blind
decisions.reason: Readable says what a covered heart means (m1).

records.literal_gloss: You will pursue in anger and destroy them from under [the] heavens of Yahweh.

en.L: Pursue [them] in anger and destroy them \q from under the heavens of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Chase them down in anger and destroy them \q from beneath the heavens of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Chase them in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger and destroy them. \q Wipe them out from under {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s sky.

pt.L: Persegue[-os] com ira e destrói-os \q de debaixo dos céus {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}.
pt.B: Persegue-os com ira e destrói-os \q de debaixo dos céus {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}.
pt.R: Persegue-os na {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} ira e destrói-os. \q Apaga-os de debaixo do céu {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}.

decisions.choice: the heavens of the LORD: God named in the third person
decisions.reason: The prayer is spoken to the LORD, but it ends with his name in the third person, as Hebrew prayer can. The ancient Greek reads 'under the heaven, LORD', speaking to him; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: destroy them from under the heavens: wipe them off the earth
decisions.reason: Everything under the heavens is the whole earth (Deuteronomy 7:24; 9:14). The man asks that his people's oppressors be removed from it.

decisions.choice: pursue in anger: as God pursued his people in verse 43
decisions.reason: The same words were used of God's anger against his people in verse 43; the chapter ends with the plea that it be turned on their enemies.

decisions.choice: your anger
decisions.reason: Readable says whose anger it is; the Hebrew has 'in anger'.
